blocks.prompt: Which fruit of the Spirit did you taste most this week? Which one is God reaching to grow in you next?
blocks.placeholder: God grew _____ in me this week

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be known by love
Thank Jesus for a simple, enormous way to be recognized

intro.text: Put every picture together now: a tree planted right beside a river, roots reaching the stream, leaves green through the worst drought. This is the whole goal of the season — to live your life planted by living water.

verse.text: That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither — whatever they do prospers.

blocks.text: Psalm 1 gives us the fountainhead image of the whole season. Notice what the tree does NOT do: panic. It yields fruit in season — not in every season, but in season. It withers in no season. 'Whatever they do prospers' — not because nothing goes wrong, but because the water keeps coming and the roots stay connected.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Draw or imagine your tree planted by a river
Underline: 'fruit IN SEASON, no withering'
Name one thing that shouldn't wither in your life

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for streams that never dry
Ask to be planted, not just passing by

verse.text: They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves are always green.

blocks.text: The key phrase is 'does not fear when heat comes.' Tree-people don't deny the heat; they don't feel it the same way. The drought is real, but their supply line goes to the stream. Your anchor is what heats fear out of the picture. Read the verse again and put your own heat in the sentence.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the 'heat' (pressure, deadline, worry) in your life
Reach your root to the stream once today
Say: 'I don't fear the heat; my root is by the water'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to be your stream in this season's heat
Thank Him for leaves that stay green anyway

verse.text: They drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

blocks.text: In the wilderness, Israel drank from water out of a rock — and Paul quietly reveals who the rock was. The water that followed them through the desert was Christ. Your stream was there in your wildernesses before you even knew to look. The Rock has been accompanying you the whole time, ready to give water.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look back: when did God provide 'water' you didn't expect?
See the Rock who has accompanied you
Drink — receive from Him today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Christ, the Rock who has walked with you
Ask to know His water in your current wilderness

verse.text: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.

blocks.text: Rivers have sources, and the source of every good river is one fountain. 'With you is the fountain of life' — the spring deep behind your season. And look at the line's end: 'in your light we see light.' Everything bright you've ever enjoyed is reflected brightness. Your life's water all traces back to one living fountain.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Trace one good thing in your life back to its source
Worship at the fountain, not the stream
Say: 'with You is the fountain of life'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is the source behind all sources
Ask to keep drinking where life actually comes from

verse.text: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, they will grow like a cedar of Lebanon; planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God.

blocks.text: Quiz day — and this verse shows where the best trees are planted: in the courtyard of God's house, right where the water and the care gather. The righteous don't just survive; they flourish. Check what you remember about life by the water.

blocks.question: Where do the righteous flourish, according to Psalm 92:13?
blocks.explain: Psalm 92:13: 'planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God.' The best planting spot is near God's presence and God's people.
options: In the deep woods far from anyone
In the house of the Lord, in the courts of God
On the dry hillside where they look dramatic
In the richest soil they can buy

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to flourish where God plants you
Thank Him for a house with roots-room in it

verse.text: The Lord will guide you always; he will satisfy your needs in a sun-scorched land and will strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden.

blocks.text: Rest day for the water tree. 'Well-watered' is your identity. Even in sun-scorched land, God satisfies needs and strengthens frames — the water is not a hope, it's a promise. Today, don't work for the garden; be the garden. Let the water arrive.

blocks.prompt: When have you felt most 'well-watered'? What does your soul look like when it's satisfied instead of scorched?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Be the well-watered garden, not the worried gardener
Thank God for satisfaction in a scorched land

verse.text: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells.

blocks.text: Three weeks left — and we end the water week inside the city. The river's streams 'make glad' — not just supply, but gladden. The water tree is not sustained and miserable; it's sustained and glad. Let week 11 end with rivers making your heart glad. That's what all this deep-rooted living is for.

blocks.prompt: Where has joy come from being planted by streams? What has this season's 'water' made glad in you?
blocks.placeholder: The water has made me glad because...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the river's streams make you glad
Thank the Most High for dwelling in such a city

intro.text: A tree's story is written in its rings — wide years and narrow years, good rain and drought. This week we learn to read seasons: the time for everything, and the patience to trust God with the calendar.

verse.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

blocks.text: The most freeing calendar is God's calendar: a time for everything. A time to grow and a time to rest. A time to speak and a time to be quiet. The reason life feels out of rhythm is usually that we're trying to do one season in another — blooming in winter, sleeping in spring. Ask what time it actually is for you.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name your current 'season' — growing, waiting, pruning, resting?
Stop fighting the season you're in
Do what today's season calls for, not last month's

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you what time it is
Thank Him for a season for everything

verse.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time.

blocks.text: The same verse right after 'a time for everything' holds the comfort: everything beautiful in its time. Not beautiful on your schedule. The ring you can't see the beauty of yet is the one being drawn slowly in the dark. God sees the whole tree at every age; He declares each season beautiful at its proper time.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find one 'ugly now' part of your year and ask God to show its purpose
Trust that beauty is scheduled, not missing
Say: 'He has made everything beautiful in its time'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell God the season you can't see beauty in yet
Thank Him for a beauty that waits for its time

verse.text: Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

blocks.text: Every tree knows its days are numbered; that's why it makes rings instead of putting everything into one afternoon. 'Teach us to number our days' is not morbid — it's how you get wisdom. When you know the season has a number and a limit, you spend it on things that matter. Each day is a ring you're adding.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at a tree ring or a calendar — count ahead
Ask: am I using what's numbered like it's numbered?
Give this day a purpose worth a ring

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the wisdom of numbered days
Thank God for the days He's given you to count

verse.text: He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rains that water the earth.

blocks.text: Hard seasons end — that's the quiet promise in this verse. The Lord comes to us 'like the spring rains that water the earth.' Spring always returns to the garden. If your rings have been drought-thin for a while, there is still rain on the calendar. God's arrival refreshes; He doesn't just command the ground to try harder.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wait like a farmer for God's timing, not yours
Don't panic at the drought; watch for the rain
Say: 'He comes to me like spring rains'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for spring rain where you've been dry
Thank God that He comes as rain, not just requirement

verse.text: See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

blocks.text: Quiz day on patience. The farmer is the Bible's favorite picture of wise waiting — he doesn't check on every seed every hour, and he doesn't dig the whole field looking for progress. He waits for both rains and trusts the land. Here's today's check: how do you read your own rings?

blocks.question: In James 5:7, the farmer waits for the crop patiently. He waits for what two things?
blocks.explain: 'He waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.' The farmer trusts a rhythm he can depend on — and so can you.
options: Autumn and spring rains
Warmer days and longer nights
New tools and hired workers
Morning and evening watering

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to wait like the farmer, not like a panicked manager
Thank God for the autumn and spring of your seasons

verse.text: He made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows when to go down.

blocks.text: Rest day — and the excuse is cosmic: God timed the moon and the sun, making the whole sky a calendar of rest and rhythm. Night comes so rest can come. The moon marks the seasons so you can trust the turn. Rest beneath the order God built instead of fighting it.

blocks.prompt: What season marker have you noticed lately — the day shortening, the sky, a birthday? What is it saying about where you are?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest under God's ordered sky
Thank Him for moons and seasons that mark your life

verse.text: Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be.

blocks.text: Most great trees had laughable first rings. Job's friend Bildad — who got a lot wrong — got this line exactly right: humble beginnings, prosperous future. Your first ring doesn't dictate your last one. Sown in a small beginning, overtaking with growth — that's how God writes a season. End week 12 with hope about the rings still coming.

blocks.prompt: What is one humble beginning God might be growing now toward something thriving? What's your best guess at the 'ring' you're in?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for your humble beginnings
Ask Him for the prosperous rings He has planned

intro.text: One tree is an achievement; a grove is a community. We finish the season by standing beside each other — roots that grow toward each other, shade that shelters someone else, and a whole forest that sings.

verse.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

blocks.text: The grove's first law is Jesus' own summary of His whole giving life: the giver is the blessed one. A grove doesn't hoard its fruit or its shade; trees give away their leaves every autumn and call it a good year. As you end this season, ask what you've become — a taker in the grove, or a giver?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give something today that costs you a little
Notice whose joy becomes yours
Say: 'I am built to give, like my Lord'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the giver-hearted life
Ask to be more blessed by giving than keeping

verse.text: Yet when planted, it grows up and becomes the largest of all garden plants, with such big branches that the birds can perch in its shade.

blocks.text: The tiniest seed of the season grows into a tree big enough for birds to perch in its shade. Notice the tree's reward — birds. Not applause, not prizes, birds. The purpose of bigness is shelter. The larger your root system grew this season, the more people should be able to rest under your life.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one 'bird' — someone who needs shade
Let your maturity cast a shadow that helps them
Remember: shelter, not show, is what bigness is for

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make you big enough to shelter
Thank Him for the birds He will send to your shade

verse.text: Therefore encourage one another and build each other up.

blocks.text: Trees in a grove interlock roots; people in God's family encourage each other. 'Encourage' literally means to put courage in. A grove that doesn't speak to its trees grows a forest of loners. Your words are root connections. Say one honest, specific, building thing to someone today — it travels to their root.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one specific, sincere encouragement (not flattery)
Say it to a fellow 'tree' in your family or church
Do it again tomorrow — groves do this weekly

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your words root-connections
Thank Him for the people who build you up

verse.text: You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.

blocks.text: We end close to where we began — only now the picture is bigger. One tree becomes a garden; one well becomes a spring. The whole season's growth was never about you becoming a perfect single tree. It was about you joining a grove, a garden, a spring that waters everything around it. You are part of something with more fruit than one branch can carry.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at your season as a whole — count how much grew
See yourself as part of the garden, not the whole orchard
Say: 'I am a spring whose waters never fail'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the garden you're planted in
Ask to be a spring that feeds the whole grove

verse.text: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.

blocks.text: Final quiz of the season, and here's the question behind it: thirteen weeks of roots, and where does it all go? The answer is out, toward all people — with a special priority to God's family. A grove doesn't keep good for its own roots. Check what you remember, then let the season spill out.

blocks.question: After a whole season of growing roots, where does God's goodness travel?
blocks.explain: Galatians 6:10: 'as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people.' Deep roots did their work over thirteen weeks — now the fruit moves outward, toward everyone.
options: Backward, into saving yourself
Upward, into feeling holy
Outward, doing good to all people
Sideways, only among close friends

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to direct the season's growth outward
Thank Him for the whole family of believers to love

verse.text: Let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them; let all the trees of the forest sing for joy.

blocks.text: The last rest day of the season — and the forest itself sings. You don't need to do anything today. The grove is already celebrating. When your season ends well, the trees around you catch it. Sit with the people you belong to and let the whole forest make music.

blocks.prompt: If the trees of the forest sang for joy today, which 'tree' in your life would provide the best harmony? What song is your season singing?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Join the forest in singing
Thank God for a grove worth rejoicing in

verse.text: ...down the middle of the great street of the city. On each side of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month.

blocks.text: The last verse of the season points to the last tree of the story: the tree of life in the city, bearing fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. Everything you grew this spring — every root, every ring, every fruit — is training for that tree. The end of the season is the beginning of the eternal grove. Finish well.

blocks.prompt: Thirteen weeks done. What did God grow in you this season? What do you want to keep doing daily, even after the guide ends?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the whole season of root-growing
Ask to keep bearing fruit, month after month
